tests: One `gov accept` run (single process): all 7 lines are read and red, 39 failed, 0 passed. 2 tests are unmapped, which does not meet the requirement of no unmapped test.
discoveries: I applied the runner's own `parse_map`, `matches` and `names_a_test` (on `w2/integrate`) to the README and the collected test ids, using a throwaway script in my scratchpad. Two items in the map's test cells match no test:
- `test_w2_123_determinism.py::test_equal_vectors_are_accepted_with_that_many_requests_in_flight[1,4]` (S2)
- `test_w2_123_restart.py::test_a_server_that_answers_is_never_restarted[healthy,slow]` (S5)

`matches` compares an item that has `[...]` with the full parametrized id, so this `[a,b]` shorthand names no test. As a result:
- (1) the determinism cases `[1]` and `[4]` are unmapped (the 2), and S2 counts 1 test instead of 3;
- (2) `names_a_test` makes a named item that matches nothing fail its line, so once the code is green S2 and S5 would still fail. That is a false red.

The restart cases `[healthy]` and `[slow]` are not unmapped, because F1 maps the whole restart file, but S5 still carries the dead item.
risks: Until the package below is applied, `gov accept` cannot pass W2-123: S2 and S5 stay red whatever the implementation does, and two tests stay unmapped.
lessons: In a README map, name a parametrized test by its bare function name (`file.py::test_x`, which matches every parameter) or by one exact id (`test_x[1]`). Never use a shorthand like `[1,4]`. Run the map through `gov accept` before committing a README.
proposed_decisions:
- **P-W2-123-TD-1.** Question: may the test designer correct the two test-cell items?
- Why now: they make S2 and S5 fail whatever the code does, and leave 2 tests unmapped.
- Options:
  - (a) Apply now. In the S2 and S5 test cells, drop the `[1,4]` and `[healthy,slow]` suffixes so each item is the bare function name, which `matches` maps to every parameter. This is one README commit with `Rewrite-Reason: parametrized items in a form gov accept's matcher reads`, and no test changes.
  - (b) Defer to the merge. The lead or engineer cannot edit acceptance tests, so it would come back to me anyway.
  - (c) Re-baseline the map with one row per parameter id. This means more rows for no gain.
- Impact of (a): `gov accept` should then show S2 with 3 tests, S5 with 13, and 0 unmapped, which I'd confirm with a rerun.
- Reversibility: full.
- Cost: about 5 minutes and one commit.
- Recommendation: (a). Confidence: high, because my throwaway run of the runner's own `matches` shows each bare function name matches all of its parameters.
unresolved: Package P-W2-123-TD-1. My throwaway scripts from both briefs are still in the session scratchpad, outside the tree. Read refusals in this brief: none. No `gov retrieve` queries were run in this brief.
recommended_next_action: Approve P-W2-123-TD-1 (a), so I can fix the two test-cell items, rerun `gov accept DAEO-qzrq --json` to confirm 0 unmapped, and then merge the README into W2-123's worktree.
